paragraphs: So whichever way we look at the question, the right of slavery is null and void. It is not only illegitimate; it is absurd and means nothing. The words _slave_ and _right_ contradict each other and rule each other out. It will always be just as foolish for a man to say to another man, or to a whole people: “I make a convention with you that is entirely at your expense and entirely to my advantage. I will keep it as long as I please, and you will keep it as long as I please.”

A legion in which the younger Cato was serving his first campaign under Popilius was reorganized. The elder Cato wrote to Popilius that if he wanted his son to stay on under him, he had to administer a new military oath, since the first one had been annulled and the young man could no longer bear arms against the enemy. The same Cato told his son to take great care not to go into battle before taking this new oath. I know that the siege of Clusium and other isolated events can be quoted against me, but I am citing laws and customs. No people has broken its laws less often than the Romans, and no other people has had such good ones.
